bundles.name: Identity and Designation
bundles.description: How a product type acquires, keeps, changes and loses its identity, and how it is named and cross-referenced by the parties that trade it.
bundles.rationale: Identity is the load-bearing concern for a type-level model: GS1 makes GTIN allocation and non-reuse normative, ESPR/UNTP make model-level identifiers the anchor for passports, and medical device regimes define a distinct model identifier. Naming and partner keys are separated from identity because they are mutable and non-authoritative.

layers.name: Identifier Assignment and Scope
layers.description: The authoritative identity anchor of the type, the schemes that issue it, its scope of application, and the rules that force a new identity or forbid reuse.

findings.name: Type-level identity anchor and issuing scheme
findings.description: A product type must resolve to exactly one authoritative identity within a stated scheme. GS1 issues a GTIN under a licensed company prefix for a trade item; UNTP carries a resolvable id plus idScheme and modelNumber at model granularity; medical device regimes issue a Basic UDI-DI as the model-level identifier above the trade-item Device Identifier. Where no external authority applies, the adopting Dimension assigns a UUID or ULID, never a date or a name.

findings.name: Identifier change triggers and non-reuse
findings.description: Rules determining when a modification creates a new product type rather than a revision of the existing one, and the prohibition on reusing a retired identifier. GS1 states that a GTIN is non-reusable and permanently assigned, and applies guiding principles based on whether consumers or trading partners can distinguish the change, whether disclosure is legally required, and whether supply chain handling is materially affected.

layers.name: Designation and Secondary Keys
layers.description: Human-facing designation of the type and the non-authoritative keys through which trading partners refer to it.

findings.name: Manufacturer designation, brand and multilingual naming
findings.description: The type carries a manufacturer product designation and a brand, and often a hierarchy of root, family and type designations as in the industrial digital nameplate. Names are locale-scoped and mutable, and must not be treated as identity. Brand is a change-triggering attribute under GS1 guiding principles when the primary brand changes.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Designations and brand strings are inline attributes of the master record; the only durable artifacts they imply (label artwork, brand guidelines) are governed by the media and documentation finding rather than duplicated here.

findings.name: Secondary, partner and legacy keys
findings.description: Non-authoritative identifiers used by specific parties or channels: manufacturer part number, order code, article number, seller SKU, buyer item number, catalogue item number, marketplace identifiers and legacy system keys. UBL models these as distinct buyer, seller, manufacturer, standard and catalogue item identifications, which makes the party scope of each key explicit.

bundles.name: Classification and Declared Characteristics
bundles.description: How the type is placed within external taxonomies and how its declared technical properties are given machine-interpretable meaning, including variant structure.
bundles.rationale: Classification and property semantics are the two mechanisms that make a catalog item comparable and machine-actionable. Both are governed by independent external registries (GPC, UNSPSC, HS, IEC CDD) with their own versioning, so assignments must be recorded as dated, scheme-scoped assertions rather than intrinsic attributes.

layers.name: Classification Alignment
layers.description: Assignments of the type to commercial, technical and regulatory classification schemes, each with its own version and authority.

findings.name: Commercial and technical classification assignment
findings.description: A type is normally classified in several schemes at once: a GPC brick for retail data sharing, a UNSPSC commodity for procurement, an ECLASS or IEC CDD class for engineering, and internal merchandising categories. UNTP models productCategory as an array of scheme-scoped classification objects, which is the correct shape: multiple concurrent assignments, none privileged by default.

findings.name: Regulatory nomenclature and risk classification
findings.description: Classifications that carry legal consequence rather than convenience: HS/CN customs nomenclature, hazard and dangerous-goods classes, and regulatory risk classes such as the device risk class embedded in a Basic UDI-DI grouping. These are edition-dated: the HS is amended on a multi-year cycle with correlation tables between editions, so a type's code must be re-assessed at each edition change.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Regulatory codes are inline coded values on the master record; the binding evidence (customs rulings, classification opinions) is a document governed by the conformity-evidence finding and is referenced, not duplicated here.

layers.name: Characteristic Semantics
layers.description: How declared technical properties of the type are given stable meaning, units and measurement basis.

findings.name: Property semantics and dictionary binding
findings.description: Each declared characteristic should reference a property definition in a governed dictionary rather than rely on a free-text label. IEC CDD identifies classes, properties, values and units with IRDIs of the form RAI#DI#VI, giving every property a versioned, resolvable definition; schema.org warns that consuming applications expect specific properties rather than generic property/value pairs, so the mapping between dictionary-bound properties and well-known vocabulary terms must be explicit.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Property bindings are references into externally governed dictionaries; the dictionary content is an external registry artifact and must not be copied into this model, so this finding is deliberately reference-only.

findings.name: Declared values, units and measurement basis
findings.description: The asserted value of each characteristic at type level, with its unit of measure, tolerance, and the test method or measurement condition under which it holds. Type-level values are declared or nominal; measured values from an individual unit belong to the instance or batch. UNTP models this as an extensible characteristics structure for industry-specific parameters.

layers.name: Variant Structure
layers.description: How closely related types are grouped, how they vary, and where the boundary between a variant and a distinct type is drawn.

findings.name: Variant axes, product groups and sub-type qualifiers
findings.description: schema.org models a ProductGroup as a prototype that varies by declared axes (variesBy) and is not itself offered for sale, with members linked via hasVariant / isVariantOf. GS1 introduces a further level below the trade item: the consumer product variant qualifier (cpv, AI 22) distinguishes variants that share a GTIN. Together these establish three distinguishable levels — group, type, and shared-identity sub-variant — that a model must not collapse.

bundles.name: Packaging, Composition and Inter-Type Relations
bundles.description: The physical form the type takes in trade, what it is made of at type level, and how it relates to other types.
bundles.rationale: GS1 treats each packaging level as its own trade item with its own identifier, so packaging is a type-level structural concern rather than a logistics detail. Composition and inter-type relations are needed for compliance, spare-part supply and substitution, and each is separately sourced.

layers.name: Packaging and Physical Form
layers.description: The packaging-level type hierarchy, declared content quantities and physical envelope of the type, plus its material and component composition.

findings.name: Packaging-level type hierarchy
findings.description: Each, inner pack, case and pallet configurations of the same product are distinct trade items with separate identifiers, related by a containment hierarchy with a declared child quantity. A grouping made purely for transport or storage is a logistics unit, not a trade item, and is excluded from this model.

findings.name: Net content, dimensions and weights
findings.description: Declared quantities that describe the type as a physical object of trade: net content, gross and net weight, and the outer dimensions. GS1 guiding principles treat declared net content and material dimensional or gross weight change as grounds for a new identifier, so these values are identity-relevant rather than merely descriptive.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Declared quantities are inline attributes of the master record; their supporting evidence is a measurement or test report already governed by the conformity-evidence finding.

findings.name: Type-level component, material and substance composition
findings.description: What the type is made of, expressed at type level: component types drawn from the governing bill of material, material breakdown by origin, mass fraction and recycled content, and substances of concern. UNTP models materialProvenance with origin country, mass fraction, recycled content and hazard status; the BOM structure itself is owned by the sibling engineering BOM model.

layers.name: Inter-Type Relationships
layers.description: Typed links between product types that express compatibility, dependency and succession.

findings.name: Accessory, spare part, consumable and compatibility links
findings.description: schema.org provides isAccessoryOrSparePartFor, isConsumableFor, isRelatedTo and isSimilarTo as typed relations between products. These carry operational weight: spare-part availability is a post-market obligation in several regimes, and compatibility assertions drive substitution decisions, so each link needs a direction, an asserting party and a validity period.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Typed relations are graph edges between master records; they carry no independent document and are best held as inline referenced links so that a single relation is not duplicated on both endpoints.

findings.name: Predecessor, successor and substitution
findings.description: schema.org ProductModel defines predecessorOf and successorOf, giving an explicit succession chain between model generations. Substitution differs from succession: a substitute is an acceptable alternative in a given context, may be bidirectional or one-way, and is often contract- or market-scoped rather than a property of the type itself.

findings.name: Type-instance classification and sibling product edges
findings.description: This catalog item classifies zero or more item instances (WM-OBJ-001). It may be a component type in an engineering BOM (WM-OBJ-019). Schema.org provides isAccessoryOrSparePartFor, isConsumableFor, isRelatedTo and isSimilarTo at type level. Offers use itemOffered toward this type and must not be stored as edges of the type itself. Interoperability is alignment, not claimed conformance.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Typed edges and alignment declarations are reference data on the catalog item; neighbour models hold their own artefacts (instance records, BOM files, offer documents).

bundles.name: Lifecycle, Change Control and Applicability
bundles.description: The states a product type passes through, how its specification is changed under control, and where and when it is applicable.
bundles.rationale: A catalog item is a long-lived governed record whose meaning depends on when and where it is asserted. GS1 change effective dating, ESPR post-market passport availability and market-scoped regulatory obligations all require explicit lifecycle, versioning and applicability semantics rather than a single mutable record.

layers.name: Lifecycle and Change Control
layers.description: State model of the type, controlled revision of its specification, and the obligations that survive discontinuation.

findings.name: Type lifecycle state model
findings.description: A product type moves through governed states — draft, approved, released/available, restricted, discontinued, obsolete — that are distinct from the state of any physical unit and from commercial availability. Only the type record's own state belongs here; stock availability belongs to inventory and offer models.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Lifecycle state is an inline attribute plus an event history; the durable evidence of transitions is the change decision log and change notification artifacts already defined, so no new artifact is warranted.

findings.name: Specification change control and record versioning
findings.description: Two distinct version axes must be kept apart: the version of the described product type (a generation or specification revision) and the version of the record describing it (a data correction or enrichment). Confusing them causes false change signals downstream. Change effective dating from GS1 practice and dictionary release versioning from IEC CDD both apply.

findings.name: Discontinuation and post-market obligations
findings.description: Discontinuing a type does not end its data obligations. The identifier remains permanently allocated and non-reusable, passports and compliance data must stay accessible for the product lifecycle, and support, spare-part and recall obligations continue for a defined period after the last unit is placed on the market.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Discontinuation produces dates and obligation statements on the master record plus a change notification already defined elsewhere; introducing a separate discontinuation artifact would duplicate that notice.

layers.name: Market and Temporal Applicability
layers.description: Where and when the type's assertions hold, including jurisdictional scoping and validity dating.

findings.name: Target market and jurisdictional applicability
findings.description: Most type-level assertions are market-scoped: regulatory obligations, declared quantities, labelling and classification codes differ per jurisdiction. UNTP records countryOfProduction as an ISO 3166 code; the DPP obligation depends on the product being placed on the EU market irrespective of manufacturing location, so market scope and production location are independent facts.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Market scoping is a qualifier applied to other assertions rather than a document; the underlying authorisations are conformity evidence artifacts governed by the compliance bundle.

findings.name: Temporal validity and effective dating
findings.description: Every material assertion about a type needs an effective period distinct from the instant it was recorded or observed. Classification scheme editions change on fixed dates, identifier changes have effective dates, and passports must remain valid across the product lifecycle, so bitemporal handling is a requirement rather than an optimisation.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Temporal scoping is metadata attached to other assertions and to the change set records already defined; a separate artifact would fragment the audit trail.

bundles.name: Compliance, Conformity and Evidence
bundles.description: Type-level regulatory obligations, the parties responsible for them, and the evidence that substantiates declared claims.
bundles.rationale: Under ESPR the economic operator placing a product on the market must register its passport and keep it accessible, and UNTP structures supplier assertions as performanceClaims backed by conformity evidence. These are properties of the type, not of individual units, and require explicit party roles and evidence linkage.

layers.name: Type-Level Regulatory Obligations
layers.description: Who is responsible for the type in each market and what registered, machine-readable data must accompany it.

findings.name: Responsible economic operator and market placement
findings.description: For each market, one identified party bears the obligation for the type: the manufacturer, importer, authorised representative or fulfilment service provider. Under ESPR the economic operator placing the product on the market is responsible for registering the passport in the EU registry. UNTP models this generically as relatedParty with a defined role, which is the format-neutral shape to adopt.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Operator roles and registration identifiers are inline references and coded values; the underlying registrations are held by external authority registries and must be referenced rather than copied.

findings.name: Model-level digital product passport data
findings.description: Where a passport regime applies, the type must carry the passport data set defined by its product-group delegated act, linked from a data carrier and registered so that a unique URI resolves to it. UNTP's idGranularity makes the model level explicit and lets model-level, batch-level and item-level passports coexist without conflating them.

findings.name: UDI-DI, Basic UDI-DI and type-level certifications
findings.description: For medical devices the Device Identifier identifies labeler plus version/model and is the GUDID key; production identifiers stay off this model. EU Basic UDI-DI is implemented as GMN and is assigned independently of packaging; GTIN (UDI-DI) remains the supply-chain trade-item key. Adding or removing a certification mark that trading partners must distinguish requires a new GTIN. Schema.org hasCertification records issuer, name and rating or identification.

layers.name: Conformity Evidence and Documentation
layers.description: Declared claims, third-party attestations, markings and the technical and media documentation that supports them.

findings.name: Conformity claims, markings and technical documentation
findings.description: Type-level claims (performance, sustainability, safety) must be distinguishable from third-party attested conformity and from applied markings. UNTP separates performanceClaim (supplier assertion referencing a conformity topic, metric, standard and evidence) from independently issued conformity credentials, and models productLabel as images of certification and regulatory marks. Handover and technical documentation submodels supply the durable documents.

bundles.name: Stewardship, Provenance and Data Quality
bundles.description: Who is authoritative for the record, how each assertion's origin is tracked, how the record is validated, and who may see what.
bundles.rationale: A catalog item record is assembled from many contributors with unequal authority. GS1 data-sharing practice distinguishes the information provider from the brand owner, and passport regimes grant differentiated access by user role, so authority, provenance, quality and access must be first-class rather than implicit.

layers.name: Authority and Access
layers.description: Authoritative sourcing of the record and controlled disclosure of its contents.

findings.name: Authoritative source and stewardship
findings.description: The party that licensed the identifier (typically the brand owner) is normally authoritative for the type's core identity and declared attributes, while an information provider may publish on its behalf and distributors may enrich the record. Authority must be recorded per attribute group, not per record, because enrichment legitimately comes from non-authoritative parties.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Authority assignments are inline references and precedence rules held with the record; the mandates themselves are contracts owned by a party or agreement model and are referenced only.

findings.name: Access, confidentiality and release control
findings.description: Type records commonly mix public catalog data, partner-restricted commercial data, and pre-release embargoed data. Passport regimes make this explicit by granting access to different data according to user role, which means access control is an attribute-level property of the model, not solely a deployment concern.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Access classes and embargo dates are inline governance metadata; the audit trail they imply is a service-layer log rather than a product-type artifact.

layers.name: Provenance and Validation
layers.description: Per-assertion origin tracking and the rules that determine whether the record is fit for use.

findings.name: Attribute-level provenance and dual timestamps
findings.description: Because a catalog item record aggregates contributions from manufacturers, distributors, laboratories and scraped sources, provenance must be recorded per assertion: who asserted it, from which source system, by what method, and at which event and ingestion times. Recording only a record-level 'last updated' destroys the ability to assess trust.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Provenance is metadata bound to individual assertions inside the master record; extracting it into a standalone artifact would break the one-to-one binding that gives it meaning.

findings.name: Validation, quality measurement and conflict resolution
findings.description: A type record must be validated against structural rules, classification-driven mandatory attribute sets, dictionary-bound value domains and cross-attribute consistency before publication, and quality must be measurable over time. Conflicts between contributors need a declared resolution procedure rather than silent last-write-wins.

bundles.name: Interoperability and Projection
bundles.description: How the type record is carried, resolved and exchanged across systems and standards without changing its semantics.
bundles.rationale: GS1 Digital Link defines a normative way to express type identity in web URIs; GDSN, AAS submodels, schema.org and passport formats are alternative projections of the same type-level facts. Keeping projection separate from semantics is required by the format-neutrality rule.

layers.name: Carriers, Resolution and Exchange
layers.description: Physical and digital carriers of type identity, their resolution behaviour, and the profiles used to exchange the record.

findings.name: Data carrier encoding and web resolution
findings.description: Type identity is carried on product and packaging by barcodes, QR codes or RFID and, increasingly, by a web URI. GS1 Digital Link normalises GTINs to 14 digits in the URI path and appends key qualifiers for variant, lot and serial, while explicitly warning that applications must not assume such a URI points to a resolver. Passport regimes require the carrier to lead to the passport.

findings.name: Exchange profiles and crosswalk mappings
findings.description: The same type record is projected into several external shapes: trade-item data pools, industrial asset submodels, web vocabulary markup and passport credentials. Each projection is lossy in a different direction, so mappings must be recorded explicitly with their gaps and the conflicts they cannot reconcile, and conformance must not be claimed without evidence.

model.name: Product Configuration / Variant
model.purpose: Describe a reusable configured product definition between product family and physical instance, including selections, qualified direct properties, capabilities and contextual evidence.
model.scope_statement: The aggregate owns a versioned partial, resolved or released configuration definition and its selected-feature assertions, rule/evaluation bindings, nominal properties, lifecycle and mappings. The whole family option space, design, BOM, item, session, offer and order remain external masters.
in_scope: Definition identity, scoped aliases, selections, rules and reproducible evaluation evidence
Nominal physical properties, recognition features, capabilities and explicit use limits
Design/BOM links, effectivity, release, stewardship and loss-aware interchange
out_of_scope: Owning the full product family, solver implementation, engineering design, BOM, item instance, inventory, offer, order or session lifecycle
Automatic physical operation, certification, undisclosed customer data transfer or execution of imported rule code

boundary_notes.distinction: Family and option-space masters are referenced by revision; this root owns one reusable selection definition.
Frozen registry relation CLASSIFIES is represented by a REFERENCE with explicit classifies meaning because the research schema lacks CLASSIFIES. Nominal properties are not observed instance state.

boundary_notes.neighbor: WM-OBJ-018 Engineering Design / Product Definition and WM-OBJ-019 Component Type / Engineering BOM
boundary_notes.distinction: Engineering masters retain designs and composition. This definition binds selected revisions and applicability, not their independent lifecycles.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Offer, order, inventory and configuration session
boundary_notes.distinction: Pricing, availability, customer intent and temporal selections remain separately mastered context; a session may yield a reusable definition but is not that definition.

functions.name: Resolve family and aliases
functions.description: Resolve issuer scope and family revision before accepting a candidate definition.
outputs: Unique family and revision or explicit ambiguity
preconditions: Read access is granted
effects: No identifier is silently merged

functions.name: Materialize selected values
functions.description: Resolve inherited and computed inputs while preserving value origin and explicit unknowns.
preconditions: Options and types resolve; calculations run only in an authorized adapter
effects: Existing released values remain unchanged

functions.name: Evaluate feasibility and completeness
functions.description: Invoke a separately approved bounded evaluator and retain its verdict; this contract does not implement a solver.
inputs: Pinned rules, input digest and evaluator profile
preconditions: Supported language, authorized evaluator and execution limits
effects: Timeout remains unknown; feasibility grants no release permission

functions.name: Qualify nominal properties and capabilities
functions.description: Attach evidence-backed direct properties and limits, leaving absent measurements unknown.
outputs: Qualified physical signature and capability envelope
preconditions: Units, conditions and nominal versus observed scope are explicit
effects: No inferred present operability or safety certification

functions.name: Release a reusable baseline
functions.description: Record accountable approval only after completeness, feasibility, design applicability and policy checks.
outputs: Immutable released revision and change receipt
preconditions: No required unresolved selection; positive feasibility; release authority; expected-base match
effects: Historic revisions remain resolvable; conflicting updates are rejected

functions.name: Project a variant with loss report
functions.description: Translate only supported assertions into a versioned target profile.
outputs: Projection, digest and explicit loss report
preconditions: License and disclosure permit export; unsupported mandatory semantics cause rejection
effects: Source remains unchanged; round-trip differences are visible

functions.name: Retire with dependent-item continuity
functions.description: Preserve historical interpretation while honoring authorized retention and minimization rules.
outputs: Retired revision, successor links and minimized tombstone
preconditions: No prohibited deletion or unresolved hold
effects: Retired identity is never reassigned

composition.purpose: Resolve the versioned family and option-space master.
CLASSIFIES configured physical instances without owning their identity or state; explicit projection of frozen registry relation.
Bind the selected engineering design revision.
Bind selected BOM occurrences, quantities and alternatives.

composition.target: Offer, order, inventory and configuration-session masters
composition.purpose: Resolve commercial and customer context without copying private or volatile records.

composition.target: Schema.org ProductGroup and ProductModel; GS1 CPV 1.1; OASIS UBL 2.4
composition.purpose: Candidate projections only; preserve identity scope and publish unsupported semantics and inheritance differences.

owner_package_requirements: Declare the accountable Dimension owner and authorized product-definition masters.
Register installed specification and immutable variant revisions with namespace and digest.
Declare federation and disclosure policy before following organizational or personal links.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use owner-qualified variant IDs with stable local feature keys; a local patch keeps an explicit base revision and never impersonates the organization master.

canonicalization_rules: Freeze family/rule/value revisions; keep type, unit, absence and selection origin distinct.
A released configuration requires completeness, successful feasibility evaluation and accountable release authority; none implies safety certification.
patch_rules: Apply extension only to the authorized owning Dimension using an expected-base digest and namespaced IDs; reject conflicts rather than last-writer-wins.
Validate option references, types, multiplicities, constraints, effectivity and mapping losses before release; append change evidence.
compatibility_rules: Changed defaults never retroactively rewrite released values.
Evaluate revision versus new identity under owner and adopted external identifier policy; preserve predecessor and substitution direction.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system ID
Issuer-qualified UUID
Dimension UUID with immutable revision and digest
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Use RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and explicit UTC Z or numeric offset; preserve effective time separately from recording time.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Use evidence-type plus opaque record ID and revision; never use a bare date as identity or customer data in filenames.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Record exact-byte digest and media type; verify pinned references, refuse unsafe paths or automatic execution of imported expressions.

policies: This specification describes data and proposed operations, not an implemented constraint solver or safety approval system.
No public disclosure of confidential selections, design files or customer-specific configuration without authority.
Physical properties and operating limits remain unknown until evidence is supplied; never infer hardness, density or safety from a class name.

read: Read AGENTS.md, owner policy, pinned specification and variant revision, then only authorized family/rule/design references.
create: Reuse the active Dimension, resolve an existing family and allocate a source-qualified partial definition; record unknown values explicitly.
update: Write a new revision under expected-base concurrency check; reevaluate affected constraints and retain evidence and historical baselines.
delete: Retire by default. Check retention and legal holds and dependent instances before authorized deletion; preserve a minimized tombstone and historical resolution where required.

roles.name: Dimension owner
responsibilities: Sets storage, namespace and federated access policy.

roles.name: Product definition steward
responsibilities: Owns family binding, identifier allocation and proposed changes.

roles.name: Configuration author
responsibilities: Records selections and provenance without releasing an unapproved variant.

roles.name: Engineering reviewer
responsibilities: Checks rule verdict, nominal-property evidence, composition and effectivity.

roles.name: Release authority
responsibilities: Approves immutable baseline within delegated scope.

roles.name: Projection maintainer
responsibilities: Tests mappings and reports semantic loss without changing source meaning.

access.default_rule: Deny undeclared access; public metadata does not grant access to confidential features or linked masters.
exceptions: Time-limited approved disclosure must identify audience, purpose and redacted fields; retain provenance without revealing protected values.
audit_requirements: Record actor, Dimension, target revision, operation, authority decision and RFC 3339 time for changes and protected reads.

read_order: AGENTS.md and current Dimension owner/access policy
Pinned model specification and variant revision
Family, option/rule references and evaluation receipt
Design/effectivity, release and permitted extension process

coverage.claim: Source-grounded Vercy reviewable-draft specification of Product Configuration / Variant aggregate with 12 finding records, 7 functions, 48 questions and 9 qualified sources. Coverage includes identity, lifecycle, relationships, temporal, provenance, ownership, validation, access, interoperability, properties and retention dimensions. Operational implementation, real solver fixtures, executable instance schema, sector-specific profiles and licensed ISO clause inspection remain deferred. No external Claude or Grok research was admitted; single-provider result requires separate no-tools audit and publication hold visible in all artifacts.

The typed data elements are an information contract, not a complete executable instance-validation schema or constraint solver. No implementation conformance is claimed.

Broad physical properties and capability envelopes are proposed Vercy extensions. Every real property requires its own evidence, unit, conditions and uncertainty; no universal hardness, fragility or safety ontology is supplied.
regional_assumptions: Market, identifier allocation, safety and retention obligations must be resolved under applicable owner policy and jurisdiction; this draft grants no legal approval.
adversarial_checks: Reject a GTIN/CPV/SKU or URL treated as universal engineering identity.
Reject false collapsed with unknown or a changed default silently rewriting a released variant.
Reject solver timeout as success, feasibility as release authority or technical compatibility as commercial availability.
Reject nominal mass, hardness or capability as an observed instance property or permission to actuate.
Reject transitive Schema.org inheritance, hidden projection loss or an unlicensed normative-conformance claim.
Reject private customer selections copied into a public variant or a conflicting unguarded update.

decisions.rationale: One reusable configuration revision owns selected assertions and evaluation bindings; family, design, BOM, item, session and offer keep their own masters. Packaging standalone-mm is a separate axis.
REFERENCE explicitly carries CLASSIFIES semantics toward WM-OBJ-001 because the research relation enum has no CLASSIFIES value. No item identity or state is imported.
This model has one 120-second timeout per research provider. Historical policy attempts are not model attempts. Haiku's separate no-tools audit succeeded but no external research result was admitted.

Sources support proposed design choices at declared inspection depth. ISO public abstracts do not establish licensed-clause conformance; neither do vocabulary references establish tested implementation conformance.
The proposed property and capability contracts require evidence, units and conditions. Nominal properties do not describe an instance's observed position, condition or safety.
Four boundary notes retain external design and BOM authority. Selected composition references may qualify occurrences and quantities without taking ownership of the BOM.
Completeness, feasibility, availability and authority are distinct results. Unknown or timed-out evaluation cannot authorize release. Imported expressions require an authorized bounded adapter.
The no-tools audit cannot introduce new source claims or mandate named commercial solvers. Keep a vendor-neutral evaluator profile and defer uninspected domain standards.

decisions.rationale: The frozen result explicitly separates nominal engineering definition from observed location, mass, wear and operating state of an item. The former workstream's physical-subject assumption is not inherited.

Design identity is independent of filenames and exports. Competing drawing and model assertions stay contested until the declared design authority resolves them; the latest timestamp does not silently win.
Verification of requirements and validation against stakeholder intent are separately qualified for the design revision. Neither establishes manufactured-item safety or legal certification.
The result distinguishes machine-interpretable feature associations and tolerances from graphical annotations. Matching rendered geometry is insufficient evidence of lossless engineering exchange.
NASA guidance is domain-specific and does not impose a universal baseline workflow. NIST selected historical fixtures do not establish current tool capability or exhaustive real-product conformance.
AP242 is supported only by its public scope. The empty ASME catalogue description is excluded. ReqIF release and selected XSD declarations do not establish a tested semantic mapping.

Nested field descriptions propose an information contract, not an executable instance schema. CAD/PMI adapters, real-product fixtures and calibrated acceptance criteria remain adoption work; no implementation success is claimed.
Expected-base checks, scoped release authority, separate deviation applicability, protected disclosure and retention preserve historical interpretation. A custodian does not become design owner.
Both bounded external research attempts timed out. This audit is a separate frozen-result Codex self-check with no research tools, not an independent reviewer or a Claude/Grok answer.

publicationHolds: No independent external research or independent reviewer: Claude and Grok each timed out once at 120 seconds. Source-grounded Codex research and a separate frozen no-tools Codex self-audit are used under owner authorization. This remains reviewable-draft, not canonical.

AP242 licensed clauses and sector-specific engineering/metrology standards were not inspected. ReqIF semantic mapping and source-to-field conformance are untested. No normative standards compliance is claimed.
NIST PMI evidence uses historical selected fixtures and cannot demonstrate current software capability or universal product completeness. NASA process guidance requires local applicability decisions.

No executable instance-validation schema, CAD interpreter, PMI adapter, real design fixture or verified round-trip translator is included. Nested field groups are proposed semantics requiring implementation and tests.

Physical capabilities, tolerances, recognition and safe-use claims require product-specific evidence and qualified engineering review. Information-model validity never authorizes physical action or certification.
The adopting Dimension must instantiate actual design authority, release roles, access controls and retention policy before live engineering records are created or released.
Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.
deferredResearch: Executable field-level schema and failure fixtures for conflicting authority, stale baseline, unresolved requirement and concurrent change.
Sector-specific engineering geometry, metrology, material, interface and physical-assurance evidence.
Licensed standard inspection and version-specific CAD/PMI/ReqIF crosswalks with explicit unsupported constructs.
Native-versus-derivative real-product tests for geometry, units, tolerances, semantic annotations and requirement traceability.

model.name: Inventory Stock Position
model.purpose: Describe a source-qualified inventory quantity position by product, ownership, location, status and time.
model.scope_statement: The aggregate owns stock-position identity, declared dimension grain, measured and derived quantities, snapshot currency, reconciliation evidence and bounded operational references. It is informational, not a physical object or execution engine.
in_scope: Stock dimension tuple, custody, restrictions and quantity basis
Reservation and planned-measure semantics with source-defined formulas
Snapshot consistency, count reconciliation, lineage and governed exchange
out_of_scope: Physical product geometry or material remastered as properties of a balance
Inventory booking engine, automatic warehouse actuation and oversell guarantees
Legal title determination, financial valuation and accounting entries

boundary_notes.distinction: REFERENCE only: a stock aggregate is not a serial item or its physical characteristics.
Product identity and unit conversion master stay referenced, not copied.
Movement changes positions but is not itself the current balance; no complete event ledger is assumed.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Reservation, order, warehouse and valuation masters
boundary_notes.distinction: Position retains qualified references and quantities; execution, facility identity and monetary valuation remain external.

functions.name: Read a qualified stock position
functions.description: Retrieve stock for one declared dimension grain.
preconditions: Read permission and source contract
effects: No cross-owner aggregation or missing row interpreted as zero

functions.name: Explain availability
functions.description: Trace source-defined availability formulas without executing reservations.
preconditions: Compatible grain, units and source time
effects: No universal subtraction or physical-stock inference from future reservations

functions.name: Describe projected stock
functions.description: Keep planning-horizon estimates distinct from observed balances.
preconditions: Declared plan version and fulfillment status
effects: No delivery promise or transaction authority granted

functions.name: Reconcile count evidence
functions.description: Compare a count and intervening movement evidence before proposing an adjustment.
preconditions: Matched owner, grain, unit and time
effects: No booking from count alone; approval remains external

functions.name: Route an authorized action
functions.description: Describe a master-mediated reservation or adjustment with explicit uncertain outcomes.
inputs: Expected state and master capability declaration
preconditions: Actual delegated authority and verified endpoint contract
effects: No local property edit masquerades as execution; no blind retry after lost response

functions.name: Exchange with semantic loss report
functions.description: Map authorized stock knowledge while preserving incompatible target constraints.
preconditions: Source disclosure allowed and target constraints checked
effects: Reject unqualified signed stock to positive-only event quantity mapping

composition.purpose: Link identifiable physical items only when item-level evidence exists; aggregate remains nonphysical.
Resolve product identity and qualified unit basis.
Link authoritative stock movements without assuming complete ledger coverage.
Candidate event-evidence alignment with explicit quantity and time mapping losses; not conformance.
Describe attribution and derivation, not permissions or physical truth.

owner_package_requirements: Declare the Dimension owner and delegated inventory steward.
Register authoritative stock, product, movement and location namespaces.
Bind actual read, export, action and retention policies before operation.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Issuer-qualified position ID plus explicit dimension tuple and immutable snapshot ID; neither product code nor timestamp alone identifies the position.

canonicalization_rules: Preserve grain, unit, bucket semantics, effective time and unknown values.
Never add overlapping status buckets or hierarchy reservations without a declared aggregation rule.
patch_rules: Authorized namespaced schema extension with pinned base digest; reject incompatible unit or grain changes.
Corrections append successor snapshots and reasons; stale-base edits do not overwrite a master.
compatibility_rules: A changed bucket meaning or dimension grain needs explicit migration and new schema revision.
Lossy exchange cannot silently replace authoritative stock data.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier
Governed issuer-qualified URI or global identifier
Dimension-issued UUID with issuer context
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and explicit offset or Z; distinguish effective, recorded and counted times. Timestamps are not collision-proof identity.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Artifact-kind prefix plus stable escaped identifier and revision; timestamp may be appended for readability, not uniqueness.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Preserve exact-byte digest, source receipt and mapping version; a digest proves byte identity, not stock truth.

policies: Availability formulas and allowed negative values must be declared by measure and source.
Count evidence does not authorize inventory adjustments or legal ownership changes.
On missing access, incomplete snapshot or stale evidence preserve unknowns; do not infer zero.
Do not retry uncertain operational actions until the authoritative receipt and idempotency capabilities have been checked.

read: Read owner policy, pinned specification, source grain, snapshot currency and access scope before using quantities.
create: Create a qualified snapshot from authorized source evidence; retain unobserved and excluded dimensions explicitly.
update: Append corrected snapshots with expected-base checks and provenance; route operational actions to the authorized master and verify its receipt.
delete: Apply retention and legal-hold policies; tombstone local records with protected provenance, never cascade deletion into product, movement or organization masters.

Source-qualified stock status and nonphysical aggregate class.
Quantity, unit, precision and declared bucket semantics.
Source keys, dimension grain and observation evidence; not visual item recognition.
Six bounded proposed information operations; execution authority external.
Snapshot correction, count application and action disposition.
Effective, recorded and counted time plus freshness and completeness.
Owner, custodian, product, location, movement and order references.
Snapshot, count and reconstruction evidence.
Goods owner, custodian and data authority distinguished.
Reconciliation, incompatible quantities and incomplete-snapshot fixtures proposed.
Role and owner-scoped disclosure.
Policy-controlled preservation, correction and tombstones.
Source measure mapping with positive-only event quantity limitation.
A quantity position is informational; actual item characteristics remain referenced.
Nested schemas, adapters, real fixtures and independent external review deferred.

known_omissions: Claude and Grok each timed out once. No independent external review; Codex-only result must remain reviewable-draft.
Mutable Microsoft page revision pins remain open; Odoo stock report inspected via indexed text only after direct fetch timeout.
GS1 URL says 2.0.1 while retrieved PDF header says Release 2.0 June 2022; exact normative adapter pin and conformance remain unresolved.

Actual master authority, expected-version and idempotency capabilities must be verified by adopters; source API inspection did not establish these guarantees.
regional_assumptions: Owning Dimension supplies jurisdiction, warehouse, confidentiality and retention policies. No legal ownership or financial valuation determination is made.
adversarial_checks: Reject owner and custodian conflation.
Reject sums across overlapping buckets or reservation hierarchy grains.
Reject absent row, stale value or omitted quantity interpreted as zero.
Reject expected-receipt reservation as physical stock.
Reject a count applied without intervening movement reconciliation.
Reject signed or zero stock blindly exported as positive EPCIS QuantityElement.
Reject local edit treated as execution and uncertain-action blind retries.

supplemental_provider_attempts.admission_rule: Use only a locally schema-valid result whose sources and boundaries survive adjudication.
Use only a locally schema-valid result whose sources and boundaries survive adjudication.

boundaryDecision.rationale: A source-qualified stock position aggregates quantities at a declared grain and time. Physical item, product, location, movement, reservation and valuation masters remain distinct; frozen REFERENCE WM-OBJ-001 is preserved.

decisions.rationale: Quantity and stock grain are intrinsic; geometry and material belong to referenced physical subjects.
Source-defined hierarchy, overlap and offsets prevent naive totals; custody is not ownership and expected receipts are not on-hand.
Snapshots expose consistency and freshness; counts need reconciliation before authorized application; action effects require actual master receipts.
Evidence alignment does not imply balance reconstruction; signed and zero balances require explicit target constraint handling.
Selected source passages motivate candidate contracts; revision pins, nested schemas, adapters and real concurrency fixtures are not established.
One terminal timeout per external provider; frozen no-tools Codex self-review is not independent evidence.

publicationHolds: No independent external research or review: Claude and Grok each timed out once. Codex-only research and self-audit remain reviewable-draft, never canonical.
Mutable Microsoft revision pins remain open. Odoo stock-report evidence is selected indexed text; its direct fetch timed out.
GS1 URL 2.0.1 returned a PDF labelled Release 2.0 June 2022. Exact normative adapter version and conformance remain unresolved.
No executable nested instance schema, transactional inventory engine, reservation adapter, concurrency fixture or verified round-trip translation is delivered.
Warehouse and sector-specific conversion, quarantine, consignment, negative-stock and retention policies need specialist review.
Adopters must verify real master permissions, snapshot consistency, expected-version and idempotency capabilities before operational use.
Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.
deferredResearch: Independent external review and exact source revision pins.
Executable typed fields and negative fixtures for overlapping status and reservation hierarchies.
Concurrent counting, uncertain-action receipts and complete snapshot tests against actual inventory masters.
Loss-aware EPCIS and inventory API adapters with signed and unknown quantity fixtures.

model.name: Goods Movement / Logistics
model.purpose: Represent the governed plan and observed history of moving identified physical goods through routes, legs, custody transitions, milestones and exceptions independently of storage, interface or transport provider.
model.scope_statement: Owns movement, shipment and consignment identity and boundary, cargo and handling-unit bindings, routes, multimodal legs, schedules, observations, derived status, custody assertions, condition bindings, exceptions, ETA, replanning, regulatory-status references, projections and standards mappings while neighboring masters own physical objects and legal or commercial lifecycles.
in_scope: Movement, shipment and consignment identities, party roles, service constraints, cargo lines, package and handling-unit composition and equipment bindings
Origins, destinations, routes, ordered multimodal legs, planned and actual milestones, custody assertions, condition evidence, exceptions, ETA, replanning and delivery outcomes
Regulatory status references, identifier reconciliation, provenance, access, retention, stakeholder projections and interoperability crosswalks
out_of_scope: Sale, order, title, ownership, inventory accounting, financial valuation, contract, procurement, invoice, payment, insurance claim or customs-declaration master lifecycles
Goods, lot, product, package, handling unit, transport equipment, vehicle, vessel, aircraft, facility, location, party, organization, sensor, evidence or document master lifecycles
Universal mode-specific operations, routing algorithms, tariff rules, dangerous-goods law, sanctions, customs clearance logic, carrier liability or proof-of-delivery law

boundary_notes.neighbor: Goods, Product, Lot, Package and Handling Unit
boundary_notes.distinction: The movement binds identified cargo and versions containment or aggregation for transport, while physical and commercial object properties remain externally mastered.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Vehicle, Vessel, Aircraft and Transport Equipment
boundary_notes.distinction: A leg references the means and equipment performing or containing movement; their registration, capacity, maintenance, location and lifecycle stay external.
Parties and places are assigned interval-specific logistics roles and functions but retain authoritative identity and lifecycle in their masters.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Order, Contract, Invoice, Payment, Ownership and Inventory
boundary_notes.distinction: Commercial, legal, financial and stock records may motivate or evidence movement but are not movement events and remain typed references.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Customs, Permit, Sanction and Regulatory Decision
boundary_notes.distinction: The model binds authoritative declarations, holds, releases and permissions plus their operational effect without reproducing border-agency decision lifecycles.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Sensor, Observation, Evidence, Incident and Claim
boundary_notes.distinction: Condition streams, proof, generic incidents and legal or insurance claims retain their master records; movement stores scoped observations, summaries and resolvable links.

functions.name: Register goods movement
functions.description: Create governed movement, shipment and consignment identities with scope, parties, profile and initial revision.
preconditions: Dimension and authoritative namespaces resolve
effects: a governed logistics aggregate exists without implying dispatch or delivery

functions.name: Bind cargo and handling units
functions.description: Attach referenced goods, quantities, packages, handling units, equipment and containment versions.
preconditions: identifiers, units and parent-child constraints validate
effects: movement scope becomes explicit without importing goods masters

functions.name: Create or revise route plan
functions.description: Define origin, destination, route alternatives, ordered legs, modes, parties, means, locations and schedules.
preconditions: locations, modes and dependencies resolve
effects: a versioned plan exists while prior intent remains immutable

functions.name: Record logistics observation
functions.description: Append pickup, loading, departure, arrival, transfer, unloading, delivery or return evidence.
preconditions: actor, time, place, affected objects and source validate
effects: derived state may change under deterministic precedence

functions.name: Correct or invalidate observation
functions.description: Create an error declaration, correction or invalidating successor without rewriting the source event.
preconditions: correction authority and evidence resolve
effects: prior data remains resolvable and marked

functions.name: Record custody handover
functions.description: Append offered, accepted, rejected or disputed transfer of possession or responsibility with proof.
preconditions: roles, authority, place, time and evidence validate
effects: custody interval changes without implying title or ownership

functions.name: Record condition or integrity observation
functions.description: Attach seal, damage, shortage, temperature or other condition evidence and external telemetry references.
preconditions: device or observer, method, interval and affected scope resolve
effects: condition history becomes available without importing sensor lifecycle

functions.name: Predict ETA and replan
functions.description: Version predicted milestones and create a successor route plan with model provenance and uncertainty.
preconditions: input cut-off, method, confidence and permissions resolve
effects: prediction changes without overwriting actual events or prior plan

functions.name: Open, assess and resolve exception
functions.description: Register deviation, affected scope, evidence, candidate causes, impact, response, recovery and closure.
preconditions: classification, severity, owner and escalation policy resolve

functions.name: Bind regulatory status

functions.name: Reconcile external identifiers and events

effects: federated records link without silent merge or last-write-wins

functions.name: Issue tracking projection or export

preconditions: version, permissions, freshness and mapping resolve

owner_package_requirements: Declare the Dimension owner, movement steward, shipper, carrier and handling authorities, party and goods masters, regulatory interfaces, evidence custodian and disclosure authority.
Declare shipment, consignment, goods, package, handling-unit, equipment, vehicle, facility, route, contract, customs, sensor, document and party master systems.
Publish model, object, event, relation, identifier, location, access, retention, assurance and interoperability registries.
Pin mode, jurisdiction, dangerous-goods, customs, identifier, event-vocabulary, privacy, retention and exchange profiles.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint movement, shipment, consignment, route, leg, observation, exception and revision identifiers only in the adopting Dimension's governed namespace; preserve goods, handling-unit, equipment, vehicle, party, facility, contract, customs, sensor and document identifiers as typed external references with authority, version and time.
registry_links: Dimension-local movement, shipment, location, identifier, event, access and provenance registries

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize by registry ID, model version, authoritative logistics master ID, immutable revision, object class, scope and issuer; never use tracking number, status, place, timestamp, filename or hash alone as identity.

Keep movement, shipment, consignment, booking, cargo item, package, handling unit, equipment, route, leg, observation, custody assertion and regulatory record distinct and preserve corrections and supersession.
patch_rules: Additive extensions use a Dimension-owned namespace and declare target node, mode or cargo profile, authority, source, rationale, access, event and interoperability impact.
Breaking changes require a new version, migration and crosswalk maps, compatibility declaration and continued resolution of prior plans, events and external identifiers.
compatibility_rules: Consumers may ignore unknown additive fields only when movement identity, object class, scope, place, time kind, state, authority, provenance and access meaning remain intact.
UN/CEFACT, EPCIS, CBV, DCSA, ONE Record, WCO and IMO mappings pin source and target versions and declare transformed, omitted or non-round-trippable values.

identity_priority: Authoritative logistics master-system identifier and immutable revision identifier.
Governed globally resolvable movement, consignment, leg or event IRI.
Adopting-Dimension UUID or ULID when no authoritative external identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Record event timestamps in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit UTC offset or Z; keep requested, planned, estimated, predicted, actual, sensor, capture, record, correction and ingestion times distinct.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Name serial artifacts as {movement-id}--{artifact-kind}--{revision-or-event-id}; never use a tracking number, status, place, date, filename or hash alone as movement identity.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, byte length, issuer, source and vocabulary versions, object scope, event and record times, provenance, assurance and access marking for every retained serial artifact.

policies: The adopting Dimension declares who may plan, book, bind cargo, observe, hand over, correct, replan, classify exceptions, bind regulatory status, disclose, retain and tombstone logistics records.

Every movement assertion requires subject class and identity, cargo or equipment scope, leg or route context, place, time kind, source, authority, confidence, status and revision lineage as applicable.
Agents never infer physical occurrence, custody, title, ownership, delivery acceptance, customs clearance, compliance or claim liability from a plan, estimate, scan or status code alone.

Goods, handling units, equipment, vehicles, parties, facilities, contracts, customs records, permits, invoices, payments, sensor streams, evidence and documents remain in their owning systems and are referenced.

Automated agents may append low-risk observations, predictions, reconciliations and projections under delegation, but custody acceptance, route changes with material risk, regulatory action, consequential disclosure and irreversible deletion default to confirmation or accountable authority.

read: Resolve active Dimension, purpose, role, movement profile, object scope, time horizon, requested revision, assurance, freshness and access policy; return the minimum permitted projection.
create: Create stable movement identity, class, scope, parties, cargo references, origin, destination, period, source, authority and explicit unknowns before planning or observation.
update: Append an immutable plan, event or assertion revision with actor, authority, reason, RFC 3339 effective time and predecessor; validate identifiers, containment, route, time, evidence and access before and after mutation.
delete: Apply carriage, customs, insurance, dispute, audit, retention and legal-hold policy; tombstone eligible records or withdraw projections while preserving identity, material observations and non-cascading external references.

access.default_rule: Deny mutation and sensitive disclosure unless the active Dimension, role, purpose, movement profile, object scope, location sensitivity and field policy grant the action; expose the minimum necessary projection.
exceptions: Emergency access must be time-limited, purpose-bound, attributable, independently reviewed and unable to erase immutable movement, custody, regulatory, correction or legal-hold evidence.
audit_requirements: Log actor, role, purpose, movement and revision identity, action, decision, policy and vocabulary versions, RFC 3339 timestamp with offset, affected objects and legs, source evidence and outcome for privileged mutation, custody, regulatory use or disclosure.

read_order: Read the nearest Dimension-owner AGENTS.md, movement authority, active mode, jurisdiction, dangerous-goods, identifier, access, retention and disclosure policies.

Read this model AGENTS.md, pinned spec.yaml and required goods, handling-unit, equipment, vehicle, party, facility, contract, customs, sensor, evidence and document model instructions before mutation.

coverage.claim: A source-grounded reviewable draft of Goods Movement / Logistics across UN/CEFACT, UN/LOCODE, GS1 EPCIS and CBV, DCSA, IATA ONE Record, WCO, IMO, W3C provenance and IETF time standards, without a claim of universal mode, jurisdiction, dangerous-goods, customs or legal-proof completeness.

checklist.notes: Movement, shipment, consignment, booking, cargo line, package, handling unit, equipment, route, leg, event, exception and revision identities are distinct.
Object class, mode, role, event type, business step, disposition, exception, condition and regulatory profile are versioned.
The informational movement object's scope, status, route, schedule, cargo bindings and constraints are covered; physical properties of goods, equipment and vehicles remain in their masters.
Agents distinguish plan, estimate, actual observation, correction, custody assertion and external authority decision by type, source, actor, time and evidence.
Registration, planning, booking reference, pickup, movement, transfer, delivery, return, exception, correction, replanning, closure and tombstone preserve history.
Cargo, packages, units, equipment, legs, locations, parties, custody intervals, contracts, customs records, sensors and evidence use typed bindings.
Requested, planned, cut-off, estimated, predicted, actual, sensor, capture, record, correction and ingestion times remain distinct.
Origins, destinations, waypoints, facilities, read points, business locations, coordinates, functions, corridors and uncertainty are explicit.
Sources, actors, activities, methods, observations, corrections, estimates, evidence snapshots and successor revisions are linked.
Dimension owner, movement steward, carrier, handler, object steward, regulator, reviewer and disclosure authority have separate responsibilities.
Identity, containment, quantity, unit, route order, time, event precedence, custody, condition, regulatory and crosswalk checks are explicit.
Role, purpose, delegation, field-level controls, live-location sensitivity, redaction, emergency access and audit are represented.
Immutable observations, corrections, custody and regulatory evidence, retention, legal hold, withdrawal and tombstones are explicit.
UN/CEFACT, UN/LOCODE, EPCIS, CBV, DCSA, ONE Record, WCO and IMO profiles pin versions and disclose loss.

Registration, cargo binding, route planning, observation, correction, handover, condition capture, ETA, exception, regulatory binding, reconciliation and projection functions declare controlled effects.

known_omissions: Mode, jurisdiction, dangerous-goods, customs, carriage, liability, insurance, sanctions, privacy and retention profiles require exact current rules and competent review.
Goods, product, lot, package, handling-unit, equipment, vehicle, facility, party, contract, customs, invoice, payment, sensor, evidence and claim lifecycles remain in neighboring masters.
Certified field-level crosswalks, carrier-specific code mappings, routing algorithms, ETA validation suites and legal proof requirements remain future work.
conflicts: Shipment, consignment and transport movement overlap across standards; this aggregate preserves typed local concepts and requires explicit crosswalks rather than choosing one vocabulary as universal.
EPCIS and carrier tracking events are observations with business context, not automatic proof of custody, title, ownership, delivery acceptance or regulatory compliance.
Generic logistics must support multiple modes while mode-specific operational, safety and regulatory semantics remain governed profiles and references.
regional_assumptions: WCO and IMO sources define cross-border and maritime profiles, not universal requirements for domestic or non-maritime movement.
DCSA Track and Trace 2.2 specializes container shipping and IATA ONE Record 3.2.0 specializes air cargo; neither is treated as the generic ontology alone.
UN/LOCODE release content changes under an official maintenance process, so adopting Dimensions must retain directory version and status.
adversarial_checks: Reject merging shipment, consignment, booking, cargo item, package, handling unit and transport equipment solely because one provider uses a shared identifier.
Reject actual movement, custody, delivery acceptance, clearance or compliance inferred only from a plan, ETA, scan, status label or API response.
Reject last-write-wins when carrier events conflict; preserve source, event time, record time, correction lineage, confidence and deterministic precedence.
Reject an ETA or route change that overwrites actual events or the prior plan or omits model, input cut-off, confidence, authority and successor rationale.
Reject copying goods, vehicle, facility, customs, contract, payment, sensor or claim lifecycles into the movement record when authoritative typed references suffice.

boundaryDecision.status: accepted with typed logistics objects and profiles
boundaryDecision.rationale: Movement, shipment, consignment, cargo composition, route, leg, observation, custody assertion and exception form one operational context aggregate, while physical, commercial, regulatory, sensor and evidentiary masters remain external references.

decisions.rationale: Standards overlap in terminology, so the model records class, authority and mapping instead of treating carrier identifiers as universal synonyms.

decisions.concept: Cargo, package, handling unit and equipment
decisions.rationale: Transport aggregation may change without changing the goods, and equipment contains handling units without becoming their product identity.
Goods, lots, packages, equipment, vehicles, facilities and sensors retain their direct physical properties and lifecycle outside the movement aggregate.
Requested, planned, estimated, predicted, actual, corrected, record and ingestion times cannot overwrite or substitute for one another.
Status derives from append-only observations, authority, time and deterministic precedence rather than last-write-wins.
Possession, operational control, carrier responsibility, custody, stewardship, title and ownership may differ by object and interval.
A scan or EPCIS-style event is an observation with business context and is not automatic proof of physical occurrence, custody, delivery acceptance or compliance.

decisions.disposition: accepted as versioned predictions and successor plans
decisions.rationale: Predictions retain model, inputs, cut-off, confidence and override provenance, and replanning preserves original intent and actual history.
The movement records operational consequences of holds, releases, permits and certificates while border authorities own their decisions and lifecycle.
DCSA and IATA specialize ocean-container and air-cargo exchange while the base remains mode-neutral and uses pinned mappings.
Cargo, party, value, route, condition and current-location detail can be commercially, personally or operationally sensitive and requires purpose-bound field access.

The structure covers identity, composition, planning, observation, custody, condition, exceptions, actions, regulatory interfaces, validation, provenance, access, retention and interoperability, but specialist profiles still require review.

publicationHolds: Claude and Grok timed out during their bounded attempts, so independent external review is absent and explicitly waived for this published reviewable draft.

The approved relationship ledger contains no outgoing relation rows for WM-FLW-004, so proposed composition links remain draft until registry governance approves sibling identifiers and cardinalities.

Mode, jurisdiction, customs, dangerous-goods, sanctions, carriage, liability, insurance, delivery-proof, privacy and retention profiles require competent specialist review before operational enforcement.
Certified UN/CEFACT, EPCIS, CBV, DCSA, ONE Record, WCO and IMO field crosswalks, conformance fixtures, identifier mappings and event-precedence suites remain unverified.
Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.

layers.name: Packages, handling units and equipment

findings.name: Package and handling-unit containment, aggregation and split

findings.name: Requested, planned, cut-off, estimated and revised schedule

model.name: Shipment / Consignment
model.purpose: Represent one governed trade shipment or transport consignment, or an explicitly combined logistics view, with goods scope, parties, endpoints, many-to-many allocation, requirements, status assertions and correction lineage without becoming its goods, movement, handling units, documents, trace or fulfilment obligation.
model.scope_statement: Owns mandatory shipment-or-consignment semantic kind; object and revision identity; commercial, carrier, customs and party identifiers; trade and transport party-role bindings; shipment-consignment allocation; item, quantity, value and origin bindings; package, handling-unit and equipment membership references; logistics locations and movement-plan references; service, handling, dangerous-goods, temperature, security, customs and regulatory requirements; planned, estimated, predicted, observed and actual milestone assertions; shipment-scoped custody and responsibility bindings; exceptions and outcome references; qualified measures; document and evidence references; provenance, reconciliation, access, retention and loss-aware projections. Goods, products, orders, contracts, fulfilment, handling units, inventory movements, journeys, routes, services, schedules, parties, places, bookings, transport documents, customs declarations, dangerous-goods masters, sensors, generic events, chain of custody, incidents, insurance claims and evidence masters remain external.
in_scope: Shipment or consignment identity, revision, mandatory semantic kind, party and endpoint boundary, many-to-many allocation and successor lineage
Goods-item scope, package and handling-unit membership references, requirements, movement bindings, milestone assertions, qualified measures and documents
Status, exceptions, responsibility bindings, provenance, reconciliation, privacy, access, retention and interoperability
out_of_scope: Owning goods, products, orders, contracts, fulfilment, handling units, inventory movement, journey, route, service, schedule, party, place, booking, document, declaration, dangerous-goods master, sensor, trace, incident, claim, evidence or payment lifecycles

Equating shipment with consignment, item with package, package with handling unit, custody with ownership, transport status with inventory state, plan with actual movement, milestone assertion with trace event or proof of delivery with fulfilment

Performing transportation, inventory mutation, customs clearance, dangerous-goods certification, custody proof, claims determination, autonomous consequential rerouting, protected disclosure or irreversible deletion

boundary_notes.distinction: Goods Movement / Logistics is a broader flow context. Shipment / Consignment owns the bounded trade or transport grouping and its assertions; the registered parent signal remains candidate until both models are jointly reviewed.

Shipment / Consignment records membership, loading, marks and seals. Handling-unit identity, physical properties, nesting, condition and lifecycle remain externally mastered; CONTAINS is accepted only as typed membership.

boundary_notes.neighbor: WM-FLW-009 Journey / Trip and WM-FLW-010 Route / Itinerary
boundary_notes.distinction: Shipment / Consignment binds planned or actual transport references and milestones. Journey execution, route geometry, movement observations and outcomes remain externally mastered.
A shipment milestone may cause or correlate with inventory movement, but stock ledger, location balance, reservation and inventory adjustment remain Inventory Movement concerns.

boundary_notes.neighbor: WM-FLW-013 Supply-chain Trace / Chain of Custody
boundary_notes.distinction: The model binds source-qualified milestones and current custody or responsibility assertions. Cross-organizational event graph, chain-of-custody proof and trace-query lifecycle remain in the trace pattern.
Fulfilment may reference shipments as physical delivery evidence. Commercial obligation, acceptance, proof evaluation, remedies and fulfilment outcome remain externally mastered.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Transport document, Customs declaration and Insurance claim
boundary_notes.distinction: Shipping instructions, waybills, bills of lading, declarations and claims are independently governed records referenced by the shipment or consignment; their issuance, legal effect and adjudication are external.

dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint shipment, consignment, revision, allocation, item-binding, milestone-assertion, exception and projection identifiers only in the adopting Dimension namespace; preserve external master identities as typed references.
registry_links: Dimension-local shipment, consignment, allocation, identifier, status, access, retention and provenance registries

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize by registry ID, model version, mandatory semantic kind, authoritative master ID, immutable revision, party and endpoint boundary, item scope and source profile; never use date, tracking number, document number, barcode, endpoint pair or hash alone as identity.

Keep trade shipment, transport consignment, goods item, consignment item, package, handling unit, transport equipment, inventory movement, journey, trace event, delivery obligation and transport document distinct and preserve allocations, corrections and successors.
patch_rules: Additive extensions use a Dimension-owned namespace and declare target node, trade, mode or jurisdiction profile, authority, source, rationale, access, time and interoperability impact.
Breaking changes require a new version, migration and crosswalk maps, compatibility declaration and continued resolution of prior object revisions, allocations and identifiers.
compatibility_rules: Consumers may ignore unknown additive fields only when kind, identity, item allocation, parties, endpoints, clocks, status, authority, provenance and access meaning remain intact.
UN/CEFACT, WCO, UBL, GS1, IATA, DCSA, eFTI, UN/LOCODE, units and provenance mappings pin source and target versions and declare transformed, omitted or non-round-trippable values.

identity_priority: Authoritative shipment or consignment master-system identifier and immutable revision.
Governed globally resolvable shipment, consignment, allocation or milestone IRI.
Adopting-Dimension UUID or ULID when no authoritative external identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Record event timestamps in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit UTC offset or Z; keep planned, estimated, predicted, observed, actual, record, correction and ingestion times distinct.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Name serial artifacts as {shipment-or-consignment-id}--{artifact-kind}--{revision-or-event-id}; never use a date, tracking code, document number, barcode, party, location, filename or hash alone as identity.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, byte length, issuer, source and vocabulary versions, object scope, event and record times, provenance, assurance, license and access marking for each retained serial artifact.

policies: The adopting Dimension declares who may create, allocate, compose, bind, instruct, assert status, correct, disclose, retain and tombstone shipment or consignment records.

Every assertion requires mandatory semantic kind, identity and revision, item or logistics scope, party and endpoint context, time kind, source, authority, confidence, status and lineage as applicable.

Agents never infer ownership, custody, fulfilment, inventory state, legal permission, customs clearance, safe handling, delivery completion or claim validity from a status, tracking code, document or location alone.

Goods, orders, fulfilment, handling units, inventory movements, journeys, routes, services, parties, locations, contracts, bookings, documents, declarations, dangerous-goods masters, sensors, trace, incidents, claims and evidence remain external masters.

Automated agents may append low-risk memberships, status assertions, reconciliations and projections under delegation, but custody transfer, customs declaration, dangerous-goods decisions, protected disclosure and irreversible deletion require accountable authority.

create: Create stable identity, mandatory kind, party and endpoint boundary, item scope, source, authority and explicit unknowns before adding allocations, units or milestone assertions.
